propositions: Fixture setup consumes 47% of tests/interfaces wall-clock (361.4s of 1385s) due to 589 function-scoped rebar_repo instances each running git init and related subprocess calls (306ms and 58 processes per test).

The session-scoped template approach reduces per-test setup from 306ms to 22.3ms (13.7x speedup) by building once per xdist worker and copying via shutil.copytree, but requires four fixups: rewriting worktree pointers to the copy's realpath, setting REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR per test to isolate snapshot store keys, unconditionally re-randomizing .env-id and .signing-key, and resetting the _pending_cache module global.

Bare git worktree repair inside a copy is a silent no-op that leaves the copy bound to the template's object store, making the isolation guard unable to detect it; the guard must use git worktree list --porcelain (not --git-common-dir) to reject stale pointer configurations.

The template fixture must build inside a MonkeyPatch context that pins REBAR_ROOT, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, and deletes REBAR_TRACKER_DIR/BRANCH/CONFIG to prevent per-test environment autouse contamination from reaching the template.

Deliberate coverage of the build-from-scratch path is preserved in tests/interfaces/store/test_init_idempotent_scratch.py and tests/interfaces/store/test_e4_init.py; test_rebar_repo_isolation.py provides durable sentinel checks that a half-fixed copy is rejected and no template path leaks into copied files.

An autouse tier-wide guard must verify that all paths in git worktree list --porcelain for any .tickets-tracker linked worktree resolve inside REBAR_ROOT, catching any stale pointer configuration including those left by bare worktree repair.
